chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who is praying and a woman who is praying parallel to him or to his side, he said: If her prostration is simultaneous with his bowing, there is no problem.

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a woman to pray parallel to a man in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of a woman praying parallel to a man, contingent upon the specific synchronization of her prostration with his bowing. This condition highlights the distinct spatial and temporal dynamics of the female prayer posture in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from the male arrangement where the woman typically stands directly behind. The ruling underscores the importance of maintaining proper alignment and modesty within the congregational prayer structure.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from the one who reported it,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the man who is praying Salāt and the woman is praying Salāt parallel to him or to his side. So heasws said: ‘If she was performing Sajdah along with his Rukū, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from those who he has mentioned who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a woman who performs Salah (prayer) on the side or parallel with a man. He (the Imam) said, ‘If her Sujud (prostration) is with his Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees), it is not harmful.’” (Ahadith 1-7 of this [chapter=Chapter are best explained by fatwa.)
